exothermic-reaction.context: A flask with bubbling liquid, wavy heat lines and arrows pointing out. Used for chemistry lessons on reactions that release heat, energy diagrams and lab safety.

endothermic-reaction.context: A flask with a snowflake and arrows pointing inward. Used for chemistry lessons on reactions that absorb heat, cold packs and thermochemistry diagrams.

chemical-spill.context: A tipped beaker with liquid spreading into a puddle. Used for lab accident warnings, spill cleanup procedures and chemical safety notices.

baking-soda-volcano.context: A model volcano cone with foam bubbling over its crater. Used for science fair projects, kids chemistry experiments and acid and base demonstrations.

crystal-growing-jar.context: A jar with a pencil across the rim and a string hanging into it, covered in crystals. Used for growing salt or sugar crystals at home and in classrooms.

titration.context: A burette dripping a drop into a conical flask. Used for chemistry labs measuring concentration, acid and base analysis and analytical chemistry.

flammable-hazard.context: A diamond warning sign with a flame over a bar. Used on labels and safety sheets for flammable liquids, gases and solids.

corrosive-hazard.context: A diamond warning sign with liquid dripping from tubes onto a hand and a metal bar. Used on labels for acids, bases and materials that burn skin or metal.

toxic-hazard.context: A diamond warning sign with a skull and crossbones. Used on labels for poisons and acutely toxic chemicals.

oxidizer-hazard.context: A diamond warning sign with a flame above a circle. Used on labels for oxidizing materials that feed fires.

explosive-hazard.context: A diamond warning sign with a bursting ball and flying fragments. Used on labels for explosives, fireworks and unstable chemicals.

compressed-gas-hazard.context: A diamond warning sign with a gas cylinder lying on its side. Used on labels for pressurized gas bottles and tanks.

health-hazard.context: A diamond warning sign with a person's upper body and a starburst on the chest. Used on labels for chemicals that harm long-term health, such as carcinogens.

environmental-hazard.context: A diamond warning sign with a bare tree and a dead fish. Used on labels for chemicals harmful to wildlife and waterways.

irritant-hazard.context: A diamond warning sign with a bold exclamation mark. Used on labels for chemicals that irritate skin and eyes or cause mild harm.

laser-hazard.context: A warning triangle with a starburst and a single ray line. Used on signs and labels for laser radiation areas and equipment.

atomic-nucleus.context: A tight cluster of balls, some plain and some marked with plus signs. Used for atomic structure lessons, nuclear physics and diagrams of protons and neutrons.

electron.context: A small ball with a minus sign trailing a short curved orbit line. Used for atomic structure, electricity and charge lessons.

proton.context: A ball with a plus sign inside and a subtle shine. Used for atomic structure, chemistry and positive charge lessons.

neutron.context: A ring with a zero in its centre, showing a particle with no charge. Used for atomic structure and nuclear physics lessons.

photon.context: A wavy line ending in an arrowhead with a small spark at the tip. Used for light, quantum physics and electromagnetic radiation topics.

quarks.context: A circle holding three small dots joined by springy lines. Used for particle physics, protons and neutrons made of quarks, and the strong force.

nuclear-fission.context: A small ball striking a larger nucleus that splits into two halves with smaller balls flying off. Used for nuclear power, atomic energy and chain reaction lessons.

nuclear-fusion.context: Two small nuclei colliding from each side and merging into one with a burst of energy. Used for stars, fusion power and nuclear physics topics.

half-life.context: A decay curve on axes that halves at each step. Used for radioactive decay, carbon dating and exponential decay lessons.

particle-accelerator.context: A large ring with a small ball travelling around it and a motion trail. Used for particle physics, colliders and big science facilities.

particle-collision.context: A starburst of curved and straight track lines radiating from a single point. Used for collider events, particle physics results and bubble chamber images.

quantum-entanglement.context: Two spheres with spin arrows joined by a wavy line. Used for quantum physics, quantum computing and linked particles.

gravitational-wave.context: Two small dots orbiting each other at the centre of expanding ripple rings. Used for astrophysics, black hole mergers and spacetime topics.

cathode-ray-tube.context: A glass tube with a narrow neck and a wide end, with a beam crossing to a glowing spot. Used for physics history, old television screens and electron beam demonstrations.

brownian-motion.context: One highlighted dot with a jagged zigzag path among smaller dots. Used for diffusion, molecular motion and random walk topics.

inclined-plane.context: A ramp with a box resting on the slope and an arrow pointing up the slope. Used for simple machines, forces on a slope and physics lessons.

wheel-and-axle.context: A large wheel on a narrow axle with a rope wound around the axle lifting a bucket. Used for simple machines, wells and mechanical advantage lessons.

free-body-diagram.context: A small square with four arrows pointing outward in each direction. Used for physics problems showing forces acting on an object.

friction.context: A block on a rough surface with a long push arrow forward and a short arrow pushing back. Used for forces, resistance and mechanics lessons.

projectile-motion.context: A ball at the end of a dashed arc launched from ground level. Used for trajectory, ballistics and kinematics lessons.

gravity.context: An apple falling with a downward arrow above the ground. Used for gravitational force, Newton's story and physics lessons.

balancing-bird.context: A toy bird with long drooping wings balancing its beak on a fingertip. Used for centre of gravity, equilibrium and science toy topics.

drinking-bird.context: A glass toy bird with a top hat dipping its beak into a glass of water. Used for heat engine demonstrations, evaporation and desk toys.

hookes-law-spring.context: A coiled spring hanging from a bar, stretched by a weight with a length arrow beside it. Used for elasticity, spring constant and force and extension lessons.

buoyancy.context: A block floating in water with a large upward arrow below and a small downward arrow above. Used for floating, Archimedes' principle and fluid lessons.

density-column.context: A tall cylinder with stacked liquid layers and a ball floating in one layer. Used for density experiments, layered liquids and chemistry demonstrations.

siphon.context: A bent tube running from a higher container over the rim down into a lower container. Used for liquid transfer, fluid pressure and aquarium or fuel draining.

capillary-action.context: Three thin tubes of different widths standing in water, with the liquid rising highest in the narrowest. Used for surface tension, wicking and plant water transport lessons.

meniscus.context: A close view of a graduated tube with a curved liquid surface and a dashed eye-level line. Used for reading volumes correctly in chemistry and lab measurement.

convection-current.context: A pot over a flame with arrows rising in the middle and falling at the sides. Used for heat transfer, boiling water and weather or mantle circulation topics.

bimetallic-strip.context: A two-layer metal strip bending upward over a small flame. Used for thermostats, thermal expansion and temperature switches.

galileo-thermometer.context: A tall sealed glass cylinder holding floating glass balls at different heights. Used for decorative room thermometers and density and temperature demonstrations.

calorimeter.context: An insulated cup with a lid, a thermometer and a stirrer poking through. Used for measuring heat in chemistry and physics experiments.

gas-piston.context: A cylinder with a movable piston on top, gas particles below and an upward pressure arrow. Used for gas laws, pressure and engine lessons.

convex-lens.context: A lens thicker in the middle with parallel rays entering and meeting at a focal point. Used for optics lessons, magnifiers and focusing light.

concave-lens.context: A lens thinner in the middle with parallel rays spreading outward after passing through. Used for optics lessons and nearsighted vision correction.

light-refraction.context: A ray entering a glass block at an angle, bending inside and leaving parallel to its first path. Used for optics lessons on bending light and Snell's law.

light-reflection.context: A ray striking a flat mirror and bouncing off at an equal angle with a dashed normal line. Used for optics lessons on the law of reflection.

periscope.context: A Z-shaped tube with angled mirrors at the two bends. Used for seeing over obstacles, submarines and simple optics projects.

camera-obscura.context: A dark box with a pinhole on one side and an upside-down tree projected on the far wall. Used for the history of photography and pinhole optics lessons.

laser.context: A rectangular emitter shooting a straight beam that ends in a small star. Used for light, optics, pointers and laser technology.

double-slit-experiment.context: Waves passing a barrier with two slits and spreading as overlapping arcs. Used for wave interference, quantum physics and light experiments.

mass-energy-equivalence.context: The equation E equals m c squared in bold letters. Used for relativity, nuclear energy and general physics or science themes.

electromagnetic-spectrum.context: One wave whose peaks bunch closer together from left to right. Used for radio waves, light, x-rays and wavelength and frequency lessons.

emission-spectrum.context: A baseline with a few sharp bright lines of different heights at uneven spacing. Used for atomic spectra, spectroscopy and identifying elements by light.

spectroscope.context: A handheld tube with a slit at one end and an eyepiece, with a small rainbow arch above. Used for splitting light into colours and analysing light sources.

doppler-effect.context: A moving dot with sound waves bunched close in front and spread out behind. Used for sirens, radar, redshift and wave frequency lessons.

wavelength.context: A sine wave with a double-headed arrow measuring the distance from one crest to the next. Used for wave physics, light and sound lessons.

longitudinal-wave.context: A horizontal coil with bunched and stretched sections and a direction arrow below. Used for sound waves, compression waves and wave type lessons.

light-meter.context: A handheld meter with a white dome sensor on top and a digital readout. Used for photography exposure, lighting checks and brightness measurement.

radiometer.context: A glass bulb on a stand with four vanes spinning on a pivot inside. Used for light mill demonstrations, radiation and science toys.

electric-circuit.context: A rectangle of wire joining a bulb, a battery and an open switch. Used for basic electricity lessons, circuit diagrams and electronics.

electromagnet.context: An iron nail wrapped in coiled wire joined to a battery. Used for magnetism lessons, science projects and electromagnetic devices.

bar-magnet.context: A rectangular bar magnet divided into two halves marked N and S. Used for magnetism lessons, poles and magnetic field diagrams.

magnetic-field-lines.context: A bar magnet in the middle with curved lines looping from one pole around to the other. Used for magnetism lessons and field diagrams.

electric-field-lines.context: A plus charge and a minus charge circle with curved lines arcing between them. Used for electrostatics lessons and field diagrams.

right-hand-rule.context: A fist with the thumb up beside a wire with a curved arrow showing the loop direction. Used for electromagnetism lessons on current and field direction.

leyden-jar.context: A glass jar with a foil band at the bottom and a rod with a ball on top through the lid. Used for the history of electricity and early capacitors.

electrostatic-generator.context: A large metal sphere on a column and base, with a spark jumping to a small ball. Used for static electricity demonstrations and science museums.

faraday-cage.context: A wire mesh cage with a lightning bolt striking beside it. Used for electromagnetic shielding, lightning safety and signal blocking.

static-electricity.context: A balloon beside a head whose hair stands up toward it. Used for static charge, rubbing and attraction experiments.

ohms-law.context: A triangle divided into three parts with V on top and I and R below. Used for voltage, current and resistance calculations in electronics.

transformer-coil.context: A square iron core with few coil turns on one side and many turns on the other. Used for voltage conversion, windings and power electronics.

voltmeter.context: An analog dial meter with a needle across a scale arc and a large V on its face. Used for measuring voltage in electronics and physics labs.
